author: human
request:
Feature request: filter the vet list by specialty. Three product decisions
come with it, made here as the product owner:

- Non-goal NG-9 is narrowed: free-text veterinarian search stays out of
  scope, but filtering the directory by an attribute it already shows is in.
  Record the narrowing the way the project records non-goal changes.
- The JSON endpoint at /vets is reinstated as a supported surface — this
  filter is its first requested capability. Mint a fresh requirement for it;
  the withdrawn REQ-VET-002 stays withdrawn and its id is not reused.
- The filter is a URL contract only. Neither surface gains a form, dropdown,
  or other page control in this request; pagination links carry the
  parameter so filtered pages stay navigable. A visible control may come as
  a follow-up request.

Both vet list surfaces accept an optional `specialty` query parameter:

- /vets.html?specialty=<name> — the HTML page shows only vets holding that
  specialty; pagination applies to the filtered list.
- /vets?specialty=<name> — the JSON endpoint returns only those vets.

Matching is on the whole specialty name, case-insensitive — not a prefix. A
specialty matching no vet yields the normal page or JSON document with an
empty vet list (HTTP 200). An empty or whitespace-only value behaves as if
the parameter were absent, like the empty owner search. Without the parameter
both endpoints behave as today. Cover the new behavior with tests.

These are all the product decisions; no further product answer will come
during the work. Where a choice still seems open, take the narrowest reading
consistent with this request and record the open question rather than
waiting.

author: product-requirements-expert
title: Reader narrows the veterinarian directory to one specialty from the address
summary: Both forms of the veterinarian directory accept an optional specialty in the request address and list only veterinarians holding it. Matching is on the whole name, ignoring letter case. The filter is a URL contract; neither form gains a page control.
acceptance_criteria: Both vet list surfaces accept an optional `specialty` query parameter: /vets.html?specialty=<name> lists only veterinarians holding that specialty, and /vets?specialty=<name> returns only those veterinarians
Matching is on the whole specialty name and ignores letter case; only the opening letters of a name match nothing
A specialty no veterinarian holds returns the ordinary page or document with an empty vet list and a 200 response, not an error
An empty or whitespace-only specialty value gives the same result as omitting the parameter, as an empty owner search does
Paging is counted over the filtered list, and every paging link on the HTML page carries the specialty forward so a filtered page stays navigable
Without the parameter both surfaces behave exactly as they do today
non_goals: a form, dropdown, or any other page control for choosing the specialty on either surface
narrowing the directory by any attribute other than specialty
notes: PRD changes made this dispatch: NG-9 narrowed with a non-goal ADR at docs/adr/2026-08-15-non-goal-veterinarian-search.md; REQ-VET-003 minted for the filter; REQ-VET-004 minted for the reinstated machine-readable listing per the owner's second decision (REQ-VET-002 stays withdrawn, id unreused). REQ-VET-004 records behavior that already ships, so this slice carries no work for it and its acceptance bullet should already pass. Root left the JSON-surface id question to me: I read 'mint a fresh requirement for it' as covering the surface itself, since the filter alone would leave the endpoint carrying no requirement again. Handoff for the design stage: docs/adr/README.md needs an index row for the new ADR - that file is outside my write scope. Two open questions recorded in the PRD rather than escalated, per the owner's no-further-answer instruction: whether a visible specialty control follows, and whether surrounding spaces are stripped from a non-empty specialty before matching (only the empty and all-spaces case is decided; the narrowest reading leaves a non-empty value untrimmed, and no acceptance criterion binds it).

author: system-design-expert
architectural_fit: The slice's shape is the existing owner-search shape: a paged derived repository query driven by an optional request parameter, with the blank value normalized at the controller boundary. Two decisions are new ground and are now recorded in docs/adr/2026-08-15-specialty-filter-as-a-repository-query.md with the rules stated in system-design.md § Persistence. First, the filter is a VetRepository query, not an in-memory narrowing in VetController: selecting which veterinarians a reader sees is a rule, and architecture-principles.md § In force (Web controller) admits none, calling a new controller rule a fresh violation not covered by the existing deviation. Second, case is normalized in the query rather than left to the column type or collation, and the filtered reads are not cached. VetRepository's existing reads are cached under one JCache cache with no size limit and no eviction, so a filtered read keyed by caller-supplied text would let an unauthenticated caller mint unbounded cache entries. Contracts rows for Vets, VetRepository, and VetController now cite REQ-VET-003 and REQ-VET-004, and the Known Defects row asserting the machine-readable route serves no requirement is retired because REQ-VET-004 reinstates it.
integration_points: VetRepository gains specialty-filtered reads alongside the unfiltered pair: a paged one for the HTML surface and an unpaged collection one for the machine-readable surface, mirroring the existing findAll()/findAll(Pageable) split
Both VetController handlers accept an optional specialty request parameter and pass it to the repository; a null or blank value selects the unfiltered read
The vet list model carries the specialty so vetList.html can carry it forward on every paging link
The machine-readable route populates the Vets wrapper from the filtered collection; the wrapper itself is unchanged

patterns.description: findByLastNameStartingWith(String, Pageable) — the paged derived query driven by a request parameter; the specialty query follows this shape but adds explicit case normalization, which this one lacks

processFindForm normalizes an absent search value to the broadest search at the controller boundary; blank-specialty normalization follows it. This is request binding, not a business rule, so it does not extend the recorded Web-controller deviation

risks.risk: specialties.name carries no uniqueness constraint on any vendor schema, so a veterinarian linked to two identically named specialty rows would be listed twice and counted twice in the page total
risks.mitigation: derive a distinct query so both the result and the derived count query count distinct veterinarians

risks.risk: acceptance criterion 6 requires the unfiltered surfaces to behave exactly as today, but a paging link that always emits the specialty parameter would change the unfiltered link output
risks.mitigation: omit the parameter from the link when no specialty applies; the existing paging assertions in VetControllerTests guard the unfiltered output

risks.risk: the specialty value is caller-supplied text reflected into every paging href; the template currently builds those hrefs by expression preprocessing (@{'/vets.html?page=__${i}__'}), which does no URL encoding
risks.mitigation: build the links with Thymeleaf's parameterized link expression so the link builder encodes the value; do not concatenate the specialty into the URL string

risks.risk: annotating the new repository reads @Cacheable("vets") would key an unbounded, evictionless cache on arbitrary caller text
risks.mitigation: the filtered reads are uncached per the ADR; the unfiltered reads keep their annotations unchanged

risks.risk: relying on H2's default matching would let the case-insensitivity criterion pass under the H2 test suite while failing under PostgreSQL, repeating the recorded owner-search defect
risks.mitigation: normalize case in the query itself so the behavior is vendor-independent

notes: Durable memory written this dispatch: new ADR docs/adr/2026-08-15-specialty-filter-as-a-repository-query.md; docs/adr/README.md index rows for it and for the non-goal ADR (the prd-entry's handoff item, now discharged); docs/system-design.md § Persistence gains the two repository-read rules, the Contracts rows for Vets/VetRepository/VetController gain REQ-VET-003 and REQ-VET-004, and the retired Known Defects row is recorded as retired. No design-doc-autofix records exist in the log, so the autofix audit is empty. Open questions carried forward rather than escalated, per the owner's no-further-answer instruction: (1) whether surrounding spaces are stripped from a non-empty specialty before matching — the PRD's narrowest reading leaves it untrimmed and no acceptance criterion binds it, but OwnerController.processFindForm strips the owner search value, so the two surfaces will differ until the owner decides; (2) whether a visible specialty control follows. One defect found in an artifact outside my write scope: docs/adr/2026-08-15-non-goal-veterinarian-search.md links ../prd.md#req-vet-003 and ../prd.md#non-goals, but docs/prd.md has no req-vet-003 heading — its requirement headings are section-level (### Veterinarian directory). The first anchor does not resolve.

author: security-reviewer
recommendations: Supply chain: build.gradle is unchanged by this slice and adds no dependency, so there is no supply-chain delta to verify. Note for the record that no NVD matching ran in this review — the OWASP dependency-check plugin is not configured in build.gradle (plugins declare java, checkstyle, jacoco, spring-boot 4.1.0, dependency-management 1.1.7, graalvm native 1.1.2, cyclonedx 3.2.4, javaformat 0.0.47, nohttp 0.0.11) and this reviewer has no network access. The declared framework version is Spring Boot 4.1.0; a human or CI should close the CVE check against the NVD. The CycloneDX SBOM task and the nohttp plain-HTTP check remain enabled.

The specialty value has no length bound before it reaches the query and the rendered links. Reach is limited — a value long enough to be interesting matches no specialty, so totalPages stays 0 and no link renders — so this is a note, not a finding. If a visible control follows in a later slice, a @Size bound on the parameter would be the cheap place to cap it.
approved_aspects: Data-access injection: the filter reaches the database only through the Spring Data derived query findDistinctBySpecialtiesNameIgnoreCase(String[, Pageable]) on VetRepository. No query text is concatenated and no request-derived value reaches JPQL/SQL as literal text, satisfying docs/security-principles.md Realization row 'Injection into data access'.

Cross-site scripting: the caller-supplied specialty is reflected into every paging href in src/main/resources/templates/vets/vetList.html, and each link is built with Thymeleaf's parameterized link expression @{/vets.html(page=..., specialty=${specialty})}. The link builder URL-encodes the value and th:href escapes the attribute; a test asserts '&' arrives as %26 and never raw. Output escaping is nowhere disabled (no th:utext, no unescaped inlining).

Template-expression injection: the change removes the last expression-preprocessing hrefs (@{'/vets.html?page=__${i}__'}) from the file; a repository-wide grep for __${ in src/main/resources/templates/ now returns nothing, so no request-derived text can reach a preprocessed expression on this surface. This closes the risk the design record flagged rather than repeating it.

Cache-key poisoning / unbounded memory: the two filtered reads carry no @Cacheable, so an unauthenticated caller cannot mint entries keyed on arbitrary text in the size- and eviction-unbounded 'vets' JCache. The unfiltered reads keep their existing annotations, so the pre-existing caching posture is unchanged.

Request binding and mass assignment: the parameter binds as a plain @RequestParam String on both handlers; no new @InitBinder, no new bound command type, no identifier exposure. Blank normalization (StringUtils.hasText) happens at the controller boundary and cannot produce a wildcard or catch-all query.

Exposed surface: no route is added. Both handlers are the existing /vets.html and /vets mappings gaining an optional parameter, so exposure is not broadened beyond the baseline in docs/system-design.md Security Context.

Secrets, logging, and errors: the diff introduces no credential-like literal (grep over the diff for password/secret/token/key/credential returns nothing), no logging statement, no System.out/err, and no new exception message, so nothing new can reach the error page that renders exception text.

Other classes checked and absent from the change: no file, path, or classpath resource is selected from request input; no deserialization entry point, @JsonTypeInfo, or polymorphic typing; no shell execution, reflection, regex, or network call; no new mutable state on the singleton controller (selectedSpecialty and findVets are stateless private helpers).

author: test-reviewer

findings.location: src/test/java/org/springframework/samples/petclinic/service/ClinicServiceTests.java:236-244 (theVetListPagingShouldCountOnlyVeterinariansHoldingTheSpecialty and its sibling tests in this class)
findings.description: The design-block (line 10) names a specific risk this repository query was written to guard against: 'specialties.name carries no uniqueness constraint on any vendor schema, so a veterinarian linked to two identically named specialty rows would be listed twice and counted twice', mitigated by 'a distinct query so both the result and the derived count query count distinct veterinarians' — the reason findDistinctBySpecialtiesNameIgnoreCase is named with Distinct rather than plain findBySpecialtiesNameIgnoreCase. No test in ClinicServiceTests persists a vet with two specialty rows sharing one name and asserts it is returned/counted once. If Distinct were dropped from the query in a later edit, no test would fail — the fixture data (src/main/resources/db/h2/data.sql) never gives one vet two same-named specialties, so the two existing new tests (theVetListShouldMatchTheSpecialtyNameIgnoringLetterCase, theVetListPagingShouldCountOnlyVeterinariansHoldingTheSpecialty) pass regardless of whether the query deduplicates.
findings.fix: Add a @Transactional test in ClinicServiceTests that persists (via the injected VetRepository/EntityManager or a @Sql script) a vet linked to two specialty rows with the same name (e.g. two 'radiology' rows with different ids), then asserts findDistinctBySpecialtiesNameIgnoreCase("radiology") returns that vet exactly once and the paged variant's getTotalElements() counts it once.

findings.description: Acceptance criterion 4 (prd-entry, line 4) and the intake decision (line 2) both state the parameter is ignored when it is 'empty or whitespace-only'. Both new tests exercise only the whitespace-only case (WHITESPACE_ONLY_SPECIALTY = "   "); no test sends specialty="" (a genuinely empty value, e.g. from an empty form field or a bare '?specialty=' in the URL). The code path (StringUtils.hasText) covers both, but the empty-string case is a documented edge case with no dedicated test case per the brief's Edge Case Coverage checklist.
findings.fix: Turn theVetListShouldIgnoreABlankSpecialtyValue (and its JSON-surface counterpart) into a @ParameterizedTest with @ValueSource(strings = {"", "   "}) or @CsvSource covering both the empty and whitespace-only values, per testing-principles.md's Parameterized Tests guidance for repetitive edge-case coverage.

findings.description: Accepting the implementer's measured caveat that dropping Distinct from findDistinctBySpecialtiesNameIgnoreCase does not fail this test: the test correctly pins the observable requirement (a vet linked to two identically-named specialty rows is returned/counted once), which is the right thing to assert per the brief's tested-as-spec principle — asserting outcome, not keyword. But the project has a standing, documented precedent for exactly this shape of gap: the design-block (line 6/10) itself flags 'relying on H2's default matching would let the case-insensitivity criterion pass under the H2 test suite while failing under PostgreSQL, repeating the recorded owner-search defect.' The theory that best explains the caveat is that the paged assertion never exercises the derived count query at all — the H2 --info log for this test shows a single content query with 'fetch first ? rows only' and one matching row, so Spring Data's no-count-query-needed optimization (content size < page size) short-circuits getTotalElements() to content.size() without ever running the separate count query DISTINCT would otherwise correct. If that is the mechanism, the keyword remains load-bearing for a page-filling result set (specialty match count >= page size) on any vendor, and this test's H2 run cannot see its absence — the same shape of vendor-invisible pass the design-block already named as a recorded risk on this exact query.

approved_aspects: Both round-1 findings are addressed at their cited locations: theVetListShouldShowOnlyOnceAVeterinarianHoldingTwoIdenticallyNamedSpecialties persists a vet with two same-named specialty rows via a real EntityManager and @Transactional fixture (no mocking) and asserts both the collection and paged reads return/count it exactly once; theVetListShouldIgnoreABlankSpecialtyValue and its JSON-surface counterpart are now @ParameterizedTest @ValueSource({EMPTY_SPECIALTY, WHITESPACE_ONLY_SPECIALTY}), covering the empty-string edge case the prd-entry names alongside whitespace-only
New test follows four-phase structure with blank-line separation, straight-line code, no phase comments, and BDD naming consistent with the host file's the{Subject}Should{Outcome} school

Hardcoded 'Ada'/'Nakamura' identity values in the new fixture helper match the host file's existing convention for irrelevant-identity literals (e.g. 'Sam'/'Schultz' at line 124-125), not a new mystery-literal pattern
./gradlew test passes for the full suite; both fix-delta test files build and run clean

author: change-grader
summary: narrow the vet directory to one specialty

blast_radius.note: Ten files but one code package: two Java files and one Thymeleaf template in vet/, two test files, five docs. One module, no sensitive paths, no new route, no dependency or build change; the unfiltered read paths and the vets cache annotations are untouched.

semantic_surprise.note: Read every production hunk and found no behavior the description would not predict: blank normalizes to null at the boundary, the unfiltered paging links still render /vets.html?page=N after the link-builder rewrite, the specialty is URL-encoded rather than concatenated, and Vet.specialties is EAGER so the new query path cannot fail on lazy init outside the view session. The discarded-and-reconstructed VetController and VetRepository are byte-identical to the round-1 approved tree (git diff 9d8799c 9a8733d touches only the two test files), so the reconstruction introduced nothing.

test_adequacy.note: Coverage is broad and behavioral, but the test-reviewer's own round-2 finding says the Distinct guard is not pinned: the paged duplicate-specialty assertion short-circuits getTotalElements to content.size() because the result never fills the page, so the derived count query never runs and dropping Distinct would fail no test while double-counting a page-filling narrowed list on any vendor. Case-insensitivity is likewise proven only against H2, the vendor-invisible shape the design record named as a recorded risk on this exact query.

reviewer_hedging.note: The round-2 approval that closed the roster carries an open clarify finding routed to the system-design-expert about the untested Distinct keyword, unaddressed at grading time; the security approval adds two recommendations, that no NVD/CVE matching ran in this review and that the specialty parameter carries no length bound before reaching the query and the rendered links.

scope_deviation.note: The doc surface is wider than a filter — NG-9 narrowed, REQ-VET-004 minted, a Known Defects row retired, two ADRs added — but each widening traces to a quoted owner decision in the intake record, and the single design revision was a path-coverage correction to the design-block, not a design change. Two genuinely open choices (trimming a non-empty specialty, a visible control) are recorded as PRD open questions per the owner's no-further-answer instruction rather than decided in code.

rationale: No behavioral surprise survived a full read of the production diff, and the reconstructed files match the approved tree byte for byte. What is left for a human is one test gap the approving reviewer named and left open: the Distinct keyword is load-bearing for a page-filling narrowed list yet no test would fail without it. Read that finding and the repository query before merging.
